2. The facts involved in the case, in short, are that Bangu Sheikh had jote right in respect of 54 decimals land under C.S. Dag. No. 7, 64 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 113, 13 decimals land under C.S. Dag No.127 and the said lands appertain to C.S. Khatian No.320, under mouza No. 13, North Rupshi, within Police Station and Sub-registry, Rupgonj, District-formerly Dhaka now Narayangonj and Bangu Sheikh had raiyati jote right in 313 decimals in total under this khatian and Bangu Sheikh had his wife Rupjan Bibi and his daughter Payrun Nessa and one Golam Hossain married the daughter of Bangu Sheikh and the said Golam Hossain had one son whose name is Kalimuddin through his wife Payrun Nessa and when Kalimuddin became major, his maternal grand father made arrangement for his marriage and Kalimuddin married Aushi Bibi and Aushi Bibi used to look after Bangu Sheikh when he became old and Bangu Sheikh out of love and affection transferred 194 decimals land under different dags namely 54 decimals land under Dag No. 7, 56 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 53, 71 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 11.3 and 13 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 127 to Aushi Bibi by way of Heba and also delivered possession to Aushi Bibi and Bangu Sheikh had also transferred 64 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 33 and 55 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 110 to his daughter Payrun Nessa Bibi and his wife Rupjan bibi and after the death of Bangu Sheikh , 64 decimals land under C.S:-Dag. No. 33- and 55 decimals land under C.S. Dag No.110 were recorded in the name of Payrun Nessa Bibi and the rest 194 decimals land was recorded in the name of Aushi Bibi alias Aushi during the preparation of C.S. record of rights and Payrun Ness Bibi Rupjan Bibi while enjoying and possessing 55 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 110, Rupjan Bibi died leaving behind Payrun Nessa Bibi as her only female successor and Payrun Nessa Bibi became the owner of 64 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 33 and 55 decimals land under C.S. Dag No. 110 and in this way Payrun Nessa Bibi became the owner of 119 decimals land under C.S. Dag Nos. 33 and 110 and Payrun Nessa Bibi died leaving behind Kalimuddin, her son, as her successor and Kalimuddin became the owner of 119 decimals land under C.S. Dag Nos.64 and 110 and Aushi Bibi became the owner of 194 decimals land under C.S. Dag Nos. 7, 53, 113 and 127 and in this way they were peacefully enjoying and possession the land with the knowledge of every one and Kalimuddin died leaving behind his only son Abdul Manaf and his wife Aushi Bibi, in respect of 11 9 decimals land which he inherited from his mother and later on Abdul Manaf died leaving behind his mother Aushi Bibi, proforma defendant No. 6 Mosammat Rabban Bibi, Yasin, Proforma defendant- No. 7, Abul Hossain, as his son and also proforma defendant No. 8, Mehar Negar, defendant No. 1 Suraiya Begum, defendant No. 2, Tunu bibi and proforma defendant No. 9 Gul Akhter as his daughters and Aushi Bibi wife of late Kalimuddin died in the middle part of the year, 1975 leaving behind Yasin and Abul Hossain as her sons and also Mehar Negar, Saraiya Begum, Tunu Bibi. and Gul Alditer as her four daughters and the plaintiffs of his suit land also the proforma defendant Nos. 6-9 are enjoying and possessing the suit land as mentioned in the schedule of the plaint as sixteen annas owners and also paying rents in the relevant department of the Government and the principal defendant Nos. 1-4 had no right, title, interest and possession in the suit land and it is to be mentioned that during the preparation of last S.A. record of right, the name of Ausha Miah, the predecessor-in-interest of the principal defendant Nos. 1-4, was wrongly recorded in fact Ausha Miah had never been in possession of the suit land and the Government had acquired some land under C.S. Dag Nos. 7, 110 and 113 and the bill for compensation for acquiring the land had been made in the names of the plaintiffs 

 5. It appears that the plaintiffs filed a suit for declaration of title and also for declaration that the record of S.A. Khatian in the name of Ausha Miah is wrong. The trial Court decreed the suit land and on appeal, the Court of Appeal below affirmed the judgment and decree of The trial COURT It appears that Rajabdi died leaving by Bangu Sheik and Atabdi as his two sons to inherit the properties left behind him and Bangu Sheikh died leaving behind his wife Rupban and three daughters Joynab, Payrun Nessa and Maju Bibi. It appears that Aushi Bibi wife of Kalimuddin, Manaf and Alam sons of Kalimuddin transferred their shares in favour of Ausha Miah in the year, 1937 by exhibit-Gl. The plaintiff claimed that Bangu Sheikh while alive, by way of oral gift handed over the property in question in favour of the wife of his grand son, Aushi Bibi. It further appears that one Aushi was in possession and in subsequent S.A. Khatian and R.S. Khatian it was shown that Ausha Miah was in possession of the suit land. The plaintiff claimed the title of the property in question on the basis of an oral gift given by Bangu Sheikh in appears that the documents as exhibited by the defendants especially the Heba deed in favour of Ausha Miah, sale deeds, the decree of partition suit etc. being documentary evidence were not discussed by the Courts below. The oral Heba in favour of Aushi Bibi could not be proved by any evidence. Therefore, oral or extraneous evidence to contradict the terms of the contents of a document is inadmissible under Section 92 of the Evidence Act. It appears that record of right is evidence of present possession and a registered kabala is an evidence of gift. In the instant case, Aushi Bibi though claimed the property by way of oral gift she could not prove the oral gift by adducing any evidence. There is nothing on record to show that she has title on the property but on the other hand, the title of the property passed on Ausha Miah by three registered documents, one is the Heba deed and two others by registered sale deeds. 

 6. The High Court Division observed that the plaintiffs failed to prove their title on the suit land and the fact that the name of Ausha Miah was recorded wrongly in the C.S. Khatian and subsequent S.A. and R.S. Khatians. Unless and until the registered deeds in favour of Ausha Miah and the C.S. and R.S. Khatians in his name are cancelled by a competent Court or by competent Authority, the plaintiff's claims will remain an illusion. The Courts below did not at all discuss the documentary evidence as exhibited by the defendants, as discussed by the High Court Division, which were admitted by the Court below without any objection. It is a clear case where the Courts below have committed an error of law resulting in an erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice, the High Court Division under its revisional jurisdiction is inclined to interfere with the concur-rent findings of the Courts below.
